On the interpretation of His words, "And among mankind is he who purchases idle talk to mislead [others] from the way of Allah without knowledge and takes it in ridicule. Those will have a humiliating punishment" (31:6):

The exegetes differed concerning the interpretation of His words, "And among mankind is he who purchases idle talk" (lahw al-hadith). Some of them said: it means one who buys the purchase known with a price, and they related a report about this from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

This is what [has been reported]:

Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Khallad al-Saffar, from Ubayd Allah ibn Zahr, from Ali ibn Yazid, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The sale of singing-girls is not lawful, nor their purchase, nor trade in them, nor their price," and concerning them this verse was revealed: "And among mankind is he who purchases idle talk."

Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: My father related to me, from Khallad al-Saffar, from Ubayd Allah ibn Zahr, from Ali ibn Yazid, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), in similar wording, except that he said: "The earnings from them are unlawful," and he also said: "And concerning them Allah revealed to me this verse: 'And among mankind is he who purchases idle talk to mislead [others] from the way of Allah.'"

Ubayd ibn Adam ibn Abi Iyas al-Asqalani related to me, saying: My father related to us, saying: Sulayman ibn Hayyan related to us, from Amr ibn Qays al-Kilabi, from Abu al-Muhallab, from Ubayd Allah ibn Zahr, from Ali ibn Yazid, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah. He said: And Isma'il ibn Ayyash related to us, from Mutarrah ibn Yazid, from Ubayd Allah ibn Zahr, from Ali ibn Zayd, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah al-Bahili, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Teaching singing-girls is not lawful, nor their sale, nor their purchase, and their price is unlawful, and the confirmation of that has come down in the Book of Allah: 'And among mankind is he who purchases idle talk...' to the end of the verse."

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: one who chooses idle talk and prefers it.

Those who said this:

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: "And among mankind is he who purchases idle talk to mislead [others] from the way of Allah without knowledge." By Allah, it is not that he spends wealth on it, but his purchasing it is his preferring it. It is sufficient for a man of misguidance that he chooses the talk of falsehood over the talk of truth, and what harms over what benefits.

Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-Asqalani related to me, saying: Ayyub ibn Suwayd related to us, saying: Ibn Shawdhab related to us, from Mutar, concerning the saying of Allah: "And among mankind is he who purchases idle talk," he said: its purchase is its preference.

The more correct of the two interpretations in my view is the view of those who said: its meaning is the purchase which is with a price, because that is the more apparent of its two meanings.

If someone says: How can one purchase idle talk? It is said: he purchases the thing possessing idle talk, or one possessing idle talk, so he is then a purchaser of idle talk.

As for "talk" (hadith), the exegetes differed concerning it. Some of them said: it is singing and listening to it.

Those who said this:

Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Yazid ibn Yunus informed me, from Abu Sakhr, from Abu Mu'awiyah al-Bajali, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that he heard Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud being asked about this verse: "And among mankind is he who purchases idle talk to mislead [others] from the way of Allah without knowledge." Abd Allah said: Singing, by Him other than whom there is no god, he repeated it three times.

Amr ibn Ali related to us, saying: Safwan ibn Isa related to us, saying: Hamid al-Kharrat informed us, from Ammar, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Abu al-Sahba', that he asked Ibn Mas'ud about the saying of Allah, "And among mankind is he who purchases idle talk," and he said: Singing.

Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ali ibn Abis related to us, from Ata', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, "And among mankind is he who purchases idle talk," he said: Singing.

Amr ibn Ali related to us, saying: Imran ibn Uyaynah related to us, saying: Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib related to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, "And among mankind is he who purchases idle talk," he said: Singing and the like of it.

Ibn Waki' and al-Fadl ibn al-Sabah related to us, both saying: Muhammad ibn Fudayl related to us, from Ata', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: "And among mankind is he who purchases idle talk," he said: It is singing and the like of it.

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam ibn Salm related to us, from Amr ibn Abi Qays, from Ata', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, the like of it.

Al-Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Anmati related to us, saying: Ubayd Allah related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Layla related to us, from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn Abbas, who said: It is singing and listening to it, meaning His saying: "And among mankind is he who purchases idle talk."

Al-Hasan ibn Abd al-Rahim related to us, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Musa related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Qabus ibn Abi Zabyan, from his father, from Jabir, concerning His saying: "And among mankind is he who purchases idle talk," he said: It is singing and listening to it.

Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: My father related to us, from Ibn Abi Layla, from al-Hakam or Miqsam, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The purchase of a singing-girl.

Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: Hafs and al-Mihribi related to us, from Layth, from al-Hakam, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Singing.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: "And among mankind is he who purchases idle talk to mislead [others] from the way of Allah," he said: The falsehood of talk: it is singing and the like of it.

Ibn Bashshar and Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, both saying: Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Habib, from Mujahid, "And among mankind is he who purchases idle talk," he said: Singing.

Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far and Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi related to us, from Shu'bah, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid, that he said concerning this verse, "And among mankind is he who purchases idle talk," he said: Singing.

Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: My father related to us, from Sufyan, from Habib, from Mujahid, who said: Singing.

He said: My father related to us, from Shu'bah, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Al-Ashja'i related to us, from Sufyan, from Abd al-Karim, from Mujahid, "And among mankind is he who purchases idle talk," he said: It is singing, and every game is idle talk.

Al-Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Anmati related to us, saying: Ali ibn Hafs al-Hamdani related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, "And among mankind is he who purchases idle talk," he said: Singing and listening to it, and every idle thing.

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us, and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: "And among mankind is he who purchases idle talk," he said: The singer, male or female, for much wealth, or listening to it, or to the like of it of falsehood.

Ya'qub and Ibn Waki' related to us, both saying: Ibn Ulayyah related to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: "And among mankind is he who purchases idle talk," he said: It is singing, or the singing of it, or listening to it.

Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Uthām ibn Ali related to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Shu'ayb ibn Yasar, from Ikrimah, who said: "Idle talk" (lahw al-hadith): singing.

Ubayd ibn Isma'il al-Habbari related to me, saying: Uthām related to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Shu'ayb ibn Yasar, who said thus from Ikrimah, from Ubayd, the like of it.

Al-Husayn ibn al-Zubriqan al-Nakha'i related to us, saying: Abu Usamah and Ubayd Allah related to us, from Usamah, from Ikrimah, concerning His saying: "And among mankind is he who purchases idle talk," he said: Singing.

Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: My father related to us, from Usamah ibn Zayd, from Ikrimah, who said: Singing.

Others said: By idle talk is meant the drum.

Those who said this:

Abbas ibn Muhammad related to me, saying: Hajjaj al-A'war related to us, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, who said: Idle talk is the drum.

Others said: By idle talk is meant polytheism.

Those who said this:

A report from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His saying: "And among mankind is he who purchases idle talk," meaning: polytheism.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His saying: "And among mankind is he who purchases idle talk to mislead [others] from the way of Allah without knowledge, and takes it in ridicule": These are the people of disbelief. Do you not see His saying: "And when Our verses are recited to him, he turns away arrogantly, as if he had not heard them, as if there were deafness in his ears" (31:7). So the people of Islam are not like this. He said: Some people say: it is among you, and it is not so. He said: It is the false talk in which they used to engage in vain chatter.

The correct statement on this matter is that it should be said: by it is meant everything in speech that diverts from the way of Allah, of what Allah or His Messenger has forbidden to listen to; because Allah, exalted is He, generalized with His words "idle talk" and did not specify some of it over others. So it remains on its generality until there comes what indicates its specification, and singing and polytheism are among that.

* *

As for His words, "to mislead [others] from the way of Allah":

It says: that which he purchases of idle talk diverts [others] from the religion of Allah and obedience to Him, and from what brings one closer to Him, such as reciting the Qur'an and remembering Allah.

The exegetes said the like of what we have said on this.

Those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, "to mislead [others] from the way of Allah." He said: The way of Allah is the recitation of the Qur'an and the remembrance of Allah when He is mentioned. And he was a man from Quraysh who bought a singing slave-girl.

* *

As for His words, "without knowledge":

It says: he did what he did of purchasing idle talk out of ignorance of what he will have in the end before Allah of its burden and its sin.

* *

As for His words, "and takes it in ridicule":

The reciters differed in reading this. The majority of the readers of Medina and Basra, and some of the people of Kufa, read "wa-yattakhidha" (وَيَتَّخِذُها) with a nominative ending (ḍamma), conjoining it to His words "yashtari" (يَشْتَرِي), as if its meaning for them is: "And among mankind is he who purchases idle talk and takes the signs of Allah in ridicule." The majority of the readers of Kufa read "wa-yattakhidhahā" (وَيَتَّخِذَها) with a accusative ending (fatḥa), conjoining it to "yuḍilla" (يُضِلَّ), in the sense of: "to mislead from the way of Allah, and to take it in ridicule."

The correct statement on this is that both are well-known readings among the reciters of the regions, close in meaning, so whichever reading the reciter uses, he is correct in his recitation; and the pronoun "hā" and the "alif" in His words "wa-yattakhidhahā" refer back to "the way of Allah."

Those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us, and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the saying of Allah: "and takes it in ridicule," he said: the way of Allah.

Others said: rather, that refers to the mention of the verses of the Book.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, who said: It is sufficient for a man of misguidance that he chooses the talk of falsehood over the talk of truth, and what harms over what benefits; "and takes it in ridicule": he mocks it and denies it. And the two of them being from the mention of the way of Allah seems more apt to me, because of their proximity to it, though the other view is not far from the truth; and taking it in ridicule is his mocking of it.

* *

As for His words, "Those will have a humiliating punishment":

He, exalted is His mention, says: These are the ones we described as purchasing idle talk in order to mislead [others] from the way of Allah. For them, on the Day of Resurrection, is a humiliating, disgracing punishment in the fire of Hell.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 31, verse 7:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when Our verses are recited to him, he turns away arrogantly, as though he had not heard them, as though there were deafness in his ears. So give him tidings of a painful punishment﴾ (31:7)

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: And when the verses of the Book of Allah are recited to this one who has bought idle talk to mislead from the way of Allah, and they are recited to him, ﴿he turns away arrogantly﴾, meaning: he turns his back on them, is arrogant in an arrogant manner, and turns away from hearing the truth and responding to it. ﴿As though he had not heard them, as though there were deafness in his ears﴾, meaning: heaviness, so that he cannot bear to hear it.

As:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us. And al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿in his ears is deafness﴾, he said: heaviness.

* *

And His saying: ﴿So give him tidings of a painful punishment﴾

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: So give tidings to this one who turns away from the signs of Allah when they are recited to him arrogantly, of a punishment from Allah on the Day of Resurrection that is painful, and that is the punishment of the Fire.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds – for them are gardens of bliss, abiding therein forever. The promise of Allah is truth, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾ (31:8–9)

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿Indeed, those who believe﴾ in Allah, so they affirm His oneness, and they confirm His Messenger and follow him, ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾, meaning: they obey Allah, acting upon what He commanded them in His Book and through the tongue of His Messenger, and they refrain from what He forbade them. ﴿For them are gardens of bliss﴾, meaning: for these are gardens of bliss. ﴿Abiding therein forever﴾, meaning: remaining therein without end. ﴿The promise of Allah is truth﴾, meaning: Allah promised them a promise that is true, with no doubt in it and no breaking of it. ﴿And He is the Exalted in Might﴾, meaning: He is severe in His retribution against the people of polytheism toward Him and those who bar others from His way. ﴿The Wise﴾ in the management of His creation.

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿He created the heavens without pillars that you see﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says: And among His wisdom is that He ﴿created the heavens﴾, the seven, ﴿without pillars that you see﴾. I have already mentioned, in what has passed, the disagreement of the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) regarding the meaning of His saying: ﴿without pillars that you see﴾, and we have clarified the correct view on that in our opinion.

⁕ Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Mu'adh ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, from Imran ibn Hudayr, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿without pillars that you see﴾, he said: "Indeed they have pillars that you do not see."

He said: al-Ala' ibn Abd al-Jabbar narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Humayd, from al-Hasan ibn Muslim, from Mujahid, he said: "Indeed they are with pillars you do not see."

⁕ He said: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, from Sharik, from Simak, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, he said: "Perhaps they have pillars you do not see."

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad narrated to us, from Simak, from Ikrimah, concerning this phrase ﴿He created the heavens without pillars that you see﴾, he said: "You see them without pillars, and they have pillars."

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿He created the heavens without pillars that you see﴾, he said: "al-Hasan and Qatadah said: Indeed they are without pillars that you see; they have no pillars."

And Ibn Abbas said regarding ﴿without pillars that you see﴾: "They have pillars that you do not see."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 31, verse 11:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿This is the creation of Allah. So show me what those besides Him have created. Rather, the wrongdoers are in manifest error.﴾

The Exalted One says: "This which I have enumerated to you, O people, that I created in this verse, is the creation of Allah, the One to whom belongs the divinity (ulūhah) of everything and the worship of every creature, the One for whom worship is not fitting and to whom nothing else is deserving. So show me, O polytheists, in your worship of Him alongside others, of the gods and idols, what the ones besides Him among your deities and idols have created, such that they deserve to be worshipped by you, so that you worship them instead of Him? Just as your Creator deserves this, and the Creator of these things that I have enumerated to you."

Similar to what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wīl) have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿This is the creation of Allah﴾: that which is mentioned of the creation of the heavens and the earth, and what He has dispersed of living creatures, and what He has caused to grow of every noble pair. ﴿So show me what those besides Him have created﴾: the idols that you invoke besides Him.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Rather, the wrongdoers are in manifest error﴾

The Exalted One says: These polytheists did not worship the idols and images because they create anything; rather, their misguidance and their departure from the path of truth called them to worship them. So they are in error: that is, they are in deviation from the truth and departure from uprightness. ﴿Manifest﴾: that is, it becomes clear to anyone who considers it, looks into it, and reflects with his intellect, that it is error and not guidance.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 31, verse 12:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And We had certainly given Luqman wisdom, [saying], "Be grateful to Allah. And whoever is grateful - then he is grateful only for [the benefit of] himself. And whoever is ungrateful - indeed, Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy."﴾

He, the Exalted, says: And We had certainly given Luqman understanding (fiqh) in the religion, intellect, and correctness in speech.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said things similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us. And al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿And We had certainly given Luqman wisdom﴾ He said: Understanding, intellect, and correctness in speech, without prophethood.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿And We had certainly given Luqman wisdom﴾, meaning understanding of Islam. Qatadah said: He was not a prophet, and revelation was not sent to him.

Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Yunus informed us, from Mujahid regarding His words: ﴿And We had certainly given Luqman wisdom﴾. He said: Wisdom is correctness. Other than Abu Bishr said: Correctness apart from prophethood.

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid that he said: Luqman was a righteous man, and he was not a prophet.

Nasr ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Audi and Ibn Humayd related to me, both saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Sa'id al-Zubaydi, from Mujahid, who said: Luqman the wise was an Abyssinian slave, thick-lipped, with flat feet, who was a judge among the Children of Israel.

Isa ibn Uthman ibn Isa al-Ramli related to me, saying: Yahya ibn Isa narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, who said: Luqman was a black slave, with large lips, and cracked feet.

Abbas ibn Muhammad related to me, saying: Khalid ibn Makhlad narrated to us, saying: Sulayman ibn Bilal narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id related to me, saying: I heard Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab say: Luqman the wise was black, of the blacks of Egypt.

Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ash'ath, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Luqman was an Abyssinian slave.

Al-Abbas ibn al-Walid narrated to us, saying: My father informed us, saying: al-Awza'i narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Harmalah narrated to us, saying: A black man came to Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab asking, and Sa'id said to him: Do not grieve because you are black, for there were three of the best of people who were from the blacks: Bilal, Muhajji' the freed slave of Umar ibn al-Khattab, and Luqman the wise, who was a black Nubian with thick lips.

Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Abu al-Ashhab, from Khalid al-Rab'i, who said: Luqman was an Abyssinian slave, a carpenter. His master said to him: Slaughter this sheep for us, so he slaughtered it. He said: Take out the best two morsels from it, so he took out the tongue and the heart. Then he remained as long as Allah willed, then he said: Slaughter this sheep for us, so he slaughtered it. He said: Take out the worst two morsels from it, so he took out the tongue and the heart. His master said to him: I commanded you to take out the best two morsels from it and you took them out, and I commanded you to take out the worst two morsels from it and you took them out. Luqman said to him: There is nothing better than them when they are good, and nothing worse than them when they are bad.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: al-Hakam narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Qays narrated to us, saying: Luqman was a black slave, thick-lipped, with flat feet. A man came to him while he was in a gathering of people speaking to them, and said to him: Are you not the one who used to herd sheep with me in such-and-such a place? He said: Yes. He said: What has brought you to what I see? He said: Truthfulness of speech, and silence about what does not concern me.

Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from a man, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And We had certainly given Luqman wisdom﴾: He said: The Qur'an.

He said: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: Wisdom is trustworthiness.

Others said: He was a prophet.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, from Isra'il, from Jabir, from Ikrimah, who said: Luqman was a prophet.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Be grateful to Allah﴾

He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And We had certainly given Luqman wisdom﴾, [saying]: Praise Allah for what He has bestowed upon you of His bounty. The phrase ﴿Be grateful﴾ is taken as an explanation of the wisdom, because among the wisdom he had been given was his gratitude to Allah for what He had granted him. As for His words: ﴿And whoever is grateful - then he is grateful only for [the benefit of] himself﴾, he says: Whoever thanks Allah for His blessings he has received, then he is grateful only for himself, because Allah rewards him abundantly for his gratitude and saves him by it from destruction. ﴿And whoever is ungrateful - indeed, Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy﴾: He says: Whoever denies Allah's blessing upon him has harmed himself, because Allah will punish him for his ingratitude; and Allah is free of need of his gratitude for His blessings, having no need for it, since his gratitude does not increase His dominion, and his ingratitude does not diminish His kingdom. By His words ﴿Praiseworthy﴾ is meant: praised in every state, deserving of praise for His blessings, whether the servant denies His blessing or thanks Him for it; and it is an intensive form transferred from the passive participle (maf'ul) to the form fa'il.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 31, verse 13–14:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And when Luqman said to his son, while he was instructing him, "O my son, do not associate anything with Allah. Indeed, association [with Him] is a great wrong."﴾ (13)

Allah, the Exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): And mention, O Muhammad, ﴿when Luqman said to his son, while he was instructing him, "O my son, do not associate anything with Allah. Indeed, association [with Him] is a great wrong."﴾ He means: it is a great error of speech.

Allah, the Exalted, says: We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents. ﴿His mother carried him, [weakening] upon weakness﴾ means: in weakness upon weakness, and hardship upon hardship. From this is the saying of Zuhayr:

* Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada regarding His saying: ﴿His mother carried him, [weakening] upon weakness﴾ — that is, toil upon toil.

That is: and his weaning is at the end of two years. It has been said that the phrase "at the end of" is omitted, being understood from the context, as in the saying: ﴿And ask the town in which we were﴾, meaning the people of the town.

* * *

His saying: ﴿that give thanks to Me and to your parents﴾

His saying: ﴿to Me is the [final] destination﴾

That is: to Allah is your return, O man, and He will call you to account for what you did of gratitude to Him for His blessings upon you, and for what you did of gratitude to your parents, and of your kindness to them, in return for the toil and hardship they bore from you in your infancy and youth, and what they did for you in their kindness and compassion towards you.

Interpreters have said things similar to what we have said regarding this, but they differed about what is meant by it. Some of them said: it refers to the carrying (pregnancy).

Those who said this:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿His mother carried him, [weakening] upon weakness﴾ — he said: hardship after hardship, and weakness after weakness.

* I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿[weakening] upon weakness﴾, he said: weakness upon weakness.

* Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada regarding His saying: ﴿His mother carried him, [weakening] upon weakness﴾ — that is, toil upon toil.

Others said: rather, it refers to the weakness of the child and its weakness upon the weakness of the mother.

Those who said this:

* Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, he said: Abu Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us, and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿[weakening] upon weakness﴾ — he said: the weakness of the child upon the weakness and frailty of the mother.

* * *

His saying: ﴿and his weaning is within two years﴾

That is: and his weaning is at the end of two years. It has been said that the phrase "at the end of" is omitted, being understood from the context, as in the saying: ﴿And ask the town in which we were﴾, meaning the people of the town.

* * *

His saying: ﴿that give thanks to Me and to your parents﴾

That is: We charged him to give thanks to Me for My blessings upon you, and to your parents for their raising you, and for what hardship they endured for you until your strength became firm.

* * *

His saying: ﴿to Me is the [final] destination﴾

That is: to Allah is your return, O man, and He will call you to account for what you did of gratitude to Him for His blessings upon you, and for what you did of gratitude to your parents, and of your kindness to them, in return for the toil and hardship they bore from you in your infancy and youth, and what they did for you in their kindness and compassion towards you.

It is mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas and his mother.

The reports transmitted on this:

* Hannad ibn al-Sari related to us, he said: Abu al-Ahwas related to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd, who said: Sa'd's mother swore that she would neither eat nor drink until Sa'd turned away from his religion. He said: He refused her, and she remained so until she fainted. He said: Her sons came to her and gave her drink. He said: When she recovered, she invoked Allah against him, and this verse was revealed: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man [to be good] to his parents...﴾ up to His saying: ﴿in this world, [treat them] with kindness﴾.

* Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, he said: Shu'ba related to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd, from his father, who said: Sa'd's mother said to Sa'd: "Has not Allah commanded kindness? By Allah, I will not eat food or drink drink until I die or you disbelieve." He said: When they wanted to feed her, they would force open her mouth with a stick and then pour [food] into it. Then this verse was revealed: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man [to be good] to his parents﴾.

* Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, he said: Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Dawud related to us, from Simak ibn Harb, who said: Sa'd ibn Malik said: "It was revealed concerning me: ﴿But if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them, but accompany them in this world with kindness﴾." He said: When I embraced Islam, my mother swore she would not eat food or drink drink. He said: I pleaded with her on the first day, but she refused and persisted. When the second day came, I pleaded with her, but she refused. When the third day came, I pleaded with her, but she refused. I said: "By Allah, even if you had a hundred souls and they left one by one, I would not abandon this religion of mine." When she saw that, and knew that I would not comply, she ate.

* Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, he said: Shu'ba related to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard Abu Hubayra say: "This verse was revealed concerning Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas: ﴿But if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them...﴾ the verse."

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 31, verse 15:

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them. And accompany them in this world with kindness, and follow the way of those who turn back to Me. Then to Me is your return, and I will inform you of what you used to do﴾.

He, dhikruhu, says: And if they strive with you, O man, your parents, to make you associate with Me in your worship of Me something else, which you do not know to be a partner of Mine, and He has no partner, exalted is He far above that, then do not obey them in what they urge you to of associating others with Me. ﴿And accompany them in this world with kindness﴾ means: accompany them in this world by obeying them in what carries no blame for you, between you and your Lord, and no sin.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And follow the way of those who turn back to Me﴾

It means: follow the path of those who repent of their polytheism, return to Islam, and follow Muhammad (ﷺ).

Those who engage in ta'wil (interpretation of the Qur'an) have said the same as what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿And follow the way of those who turn back to Me﴾, meaning: those who come to Me.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then to Me is your return, and I will inform you of what you used to do﴾

Indeed, to Me is your destination and your return after your deaths, and I will inform you of everything you used to do in the world, of good and evil, and then I will recompense you for your deeds, the good-doer among you for his goodness and the evildoer for his evil.

If someone says to us: What is the purpose of this statement being placed between the report about the counsel of Luqman to his son? It is said: That too, although it is a report from God, dhikruhu, about His counsel to His servants, and that He only enjoined it upon Luqman's son. So the meaning of the statement is: ﴿And when Luqman said to his son while he was advising him: O my son, do not associate anything with Allah. Indeed, association is a great injustice﴾, and do not obey your parents in associating anything with Him, ﴿and accompany them in this world with kindness﴾, for Allah has enjoined them both. So the statement resumes in the form of a report from God, and this meaning is contained in it. That is the purpose of this statement being placed between the two reports about His counsel.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 31, verse 16:

The interpretation of His statement, exalted is He: ﴿O my son, indeed it [i.e., the deed] is, if it should be the weight of a mustard seed and should be within a rock or [anywhere] in the heavens or the earth, Allah will bring it forth. Indeed, Allah is Subtle and Acquainted.﴾

The grammarians differed regarding the meaning of the hā' and alif in His statement ﴿innahā﴾ (indeed it). Some of the grammarians of Basra said: it is a reference to disobedience (maʿṣiyah) and sin (khaṭīʾah). The meaning of the sentence, according to him, is: "O my son, indeed the disobedience, if it should be the weight of a mustard seed..." or "indeed the sin." Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: this hā' is an ʿimād (a dummy pronoun, a supporting particle with no referent). He said: the feminine form of "takun" is used because what is meant is the grain (ḥabbah), so he gave it the feminine gender in reference to it, as the poet said:

"And he chokes on the word that he has spread, as the tip of the spear chokes on blood."

[The verse is by al-Aʿshā of Banu Qays ibn Thaʿlabah (his Diwan, Cairo edition with the commentary of Dr. Muhammad Husayn, p. 123), from a poem satirizing ʿUmayr ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Mundhir ibn ʿAbdan, when he brought him together with the poet Jahnam to trade insults. The verse is number (34). "Tashraq" means "to choke," and "ṣadr al-qanah" means its upper part; "al-qanah" is the spear. End of quote. In "Fara'id al-Qala'id, Sharh Mukhtasar al-Shawahid" by al-ʿAynī, he said: The evidence is in "sharaqat," where it is feminine though its subject is masculine, namely "al-ṣadr" (the chest/upper part); the analogical form would be "shariqa." But since "al-ṣadr," which is the first term of an idafah, is part of the second term, it takes its ruling. End of quote.]

The author of this opinion also said: it is permissible to put "mithqāl" in the accusative or the nominative. He said: whoever uses the nominative makes it the subject of "takun," and the indefinite noun may have no verb in "kāna" and its sisters; whoever uses the accusative makes the noun in "takun" an unidentified hidden pronoun, like the hā' in His statement ﴿innahā in taku﴾. A similar example is His statement ﴿fa-innahā lā taʿmā al-abṣār﴾ (for indeed it is not the eyes that are blinded). He said: if it were "in yaku mithqāla ḥabbah," it would be correct, and both readings would be permissible. As for the first opinion holder, he makes "mithqāl" in his statement accusative as the predicate and the completion of "kāna," and he said: some of them made it nominative, making it the "kāna" that does not require a predicate.

The second opinion is, in my view, the more correct of the two, because God, exalted is His mention, did not promise His servants that He would repay them the recompense of their evil deeds without the recompense of their good deeds, so that it would be said: "indeed the disobedience, if it is the weight of a mustard seed, Allah will bring it forth." Rather, He promised that He would repay each of the two doers the recompense of their deeds. Given that this is so, the hā' in His statement ﴿innahā﴾ being a dummy pronoun is more fitting than its being a reference to sin and disobedience. As for the accusative of "mithqāl," it is on the basis that "takun" has an unidentified (hidden) subject, and the nominative of it is on the basis that the predicate is implied, as if it were said: "if it is in the place of the weight of a grain," because indefinite nouns have their predicates implied; then it refers back to the place in which the weight of the grain is.

By "mithqāla ḥabbah" he means: the weight of a grain. The interpretation of the statement, then, is: "Indeed the matter, if it is the weight of a grain of mustard, of good or evil that you have done, and it be in a rock, or in the heavens, or in the earth, Allah will bring it forth on the Day of Resurrection, until He repays you for it."

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His statement: ﴿O my son, indeed it is, if it should be the weight of a mustard seed﴾ — of good or evil.

The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of His statement ﴿and it be within a rock﴾. Some of them said: he meant by it the rock upon which the earth rests. This is a view narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas and others, and they said: it is a green rock.

Mention of those who said that:

Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from al-Minhal, from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Harith, who said: "The rock is green, on the back of a fish."

Musa ibn Harun narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, in a report he mentioned from Abu Malik, from Abu Salih, from Ibn ʿAbbas, and from Murrah, from ʿAbd Allah, and from some of the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ): God created the earth upon a fish, and the fish is the Nun that God mentioned in the Qur'an: ﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe﴾. The fish is in the water, the water is on the back of a stone, the stone is on the back of an angel, the angel is on a rock, and the rock is in the wind; and this is the rock that Luqman mentioned, which is neither in the heavens nor in the earth.

Others said: he meant by it the mountains, and they said the meaning of the sentence is: "and it be in a mountain."

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His statement ﴿within a rock﴾: i.e., a mountain.

* *

As for His statement ﴿Allah will bring it forth﴾:

Some of them directed its meaning to: Allah will know it. I do not know "yaʾti bihā" to mean "yaʿlamuhu" (He will know it), unless the speaker means that Luqman only described God with this because God knows its places, and nothing of it is hidden from Him, in which case it would be a valid interpretation.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman and Yahya narrated to us, both saying: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Abu Malik regarding ﴿and it be within a rock or in the heavens or in the earth, Allah will bring it forth﴾: He said: Allah will know it.

Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi, from Abu Malik, the like of it.

* *

As for His statement ﴿Indeed, Allah is Subtle and Acquainted﴾:

He says: indeed Allah is Subtle in extracting the grain from its place wherever it is, and Acquainted with its location.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding ﴿Indeed, Allah is Subtle and Acquainted﴾: i.e., Subtle in extracting it, Acquainted with its resting place.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 31, verse 17:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O my son, establish prayer, enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and bear patiently whatever befalls you. Indeed, that is of the matters requiring determination.﴾ (31:17)

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, relating the words of Luqman to his son: ﴿O my son, establish prayer﴾ within its bounds; ﴿and enjoin what is right﴾ meaning: and command the people to obey Allah and follow His command; ﴿and forbid what is wrong﴾ meaning: and forbid the people from the disobedience of Allah and from committing what He has forbidden; ﴿and bear patiently whatever befalls you﴾ meaning: and be patient over what afflicts you from the people for the sake of Allah when you command them to what is right and forbid them from what is wrong, and let not what reaches you from them turn you away from that; ﴿Indeed, that is of the matters requiring determination﴾ meaning: indeed, that is among the matters which Allah has commanded as a matter of determination on His part.

And the people of interpretation said similarly to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, regarding His saying: (O my son, establish prayer, enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and bear patiently whatever befalls you). He said: Be patient over the harm that afflicts you in that. ﴿Indeed, that is of the matters requiring determination﴾ He said: Indeed, that is among the matters which Allah has determined, meaning: among the matters which Allah has commanded.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He: "And do not turn your cheek away from people in contempt, and do not walk upon the earth exultantly. Indeed, Allah does not like everyone self-deluded and boastful" (31:18).

The reciters differed over the reading of His words "wa-la tusa''ir" (ولا تُصَعِّرْ). Some of the reciters of Kufa, of Madina, and of the Kufans read it "wa-la tusa''ir" on the pattern of "tufa''il" (تُفَعِّل). Some of the Meccans and most of the reciters of Madina, Kufa and Basra read it "wa-la tusa'ir" (ولا تُصَاعِرْ) on the pattern of "tufa'il" (تُفَاعِل).

The correct view on this matter is to say: these are two readings, and scholars among the reciters have read with each of them, so whichever reading the reciter uses is correct. The meaning of the statement is: do not turn your face away from the one you are speaking to, out of arrogance and belittling of the one you address. The origin of "al-sa'r" (الصعر) is a disease that afflicts camels in their necks or heads, until their necks turn away from their heads; the arrogant man over people is likened to it. From this is the verse of 'Amr ibn Hunayy al-Taghlibi:

"We, when the tyrant turned his cheek (in pride), would straighten him from his inclination, and he would stand upright."

[The verse is attributed to 'Amr ibn Hunayy (with a nun) al-Taghlibi (Mu'jam al-shu'ara' of al-Marzubani, pp. 206–207), a known pre-Islamic horseman, who says, concerning their killing of 'Amr ibn Hind, according to the narration of Muhammad ibn Dawud: "We bring the kings their due, as they intended toward us, and their killing is not forbidden to us..." "I was too proud to accept from them the blood-price of 'Amr ibn Mard'ad, when they came to water, and Rumh ibn Harthami..." "And we, when the tyrant turned his cheek, we would straighten him from his inclination, and he would stand upright." He said: he means: "then you would stand upright." This verse is also transmitted from a qasida of al-Mutalammis, whose opening is: "My mother's people reproach me, and you will not see a man of noble character except that he behaves nobly..." and after it the verse, whose end is: "we straightened him from his inclination, and he stood upright." Others transmit these verses to Jabir ibn Hunayy al-Taghlibi. Abu 'Ubayda said in explaining His words (And do not turn your cheek away from people): its metaphor is: do not turn your face, nor turn your face to a side, out of pride; and from it is the "sa'r" that afflicts camels in their heads, until it turns their necks away from their heads. 'Amr ibn Hunayy al-Taghlibi said: "And we ... and he stood upright." The verse is attributed in (Lisan al-'Arab, s.v. ṣ-‘-r) to al-Mutalammis, Jarir ibn 'Abd al-Masih. He said: al-sa'r: an inclination in the face. It was said: al-sa'r: an inclination in the cheek specifically, and it may be a natural trait in a person and in the male ostrich. It was said: it is an inclination in the neck, and a turning of the face to the extent of the two sides. He has turned his cheek and "sa''aru-hu" (صاعره): he inclined it out of arrogance. Al-Mutalammis said: "And we ... and he stood upright." He says: when an arrogant man inclines his cheek, we humble him until his inclination is straightened. End.]

The people of interpretation differed regarding its interpretation. Some of them said something similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

- 'Ali related to me, he said: 'Abd Allah related to us, he said: Mu'awiya related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding "And do not turn your cheek away from people": he means: do not be arrogant, so that you belittle the servants of Allah and turn your face away from them when they speak to you.

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: "And do not turn your cheek away from people": he means: do not turn your face away from people out of arrogance.

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us, and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding "wa-la tusa''ir": he said: aversion and turning the face away from people.

- 'Ali ibn Sahl related to me, he said: Zayd ibn Abi al-Zarqa' related to us, from Ja'far ibn Burqan, from Yazid, regarding this verse, "And do not turn your cheek away from people": he said: when a person speaks to you, you twist your face and turn away from him, belittling him.

- Ibn Wakic related to us, he said: Khalid ibn Hayyan al-Raqqi related to us, from Ja'far ibn Maymun ibn Mihran, who said: it is the man who speaks to a man and twists his face.

- 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Aswad related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Rabi'a related to us, he said: Abu Makin related to us, from 'Ikrima, regarding His words: "And do not turn your cheek away from people": he said: do not turn your face away.

- I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: "And do not turn your cheek away from people": he means: do not turn away from people; he means: face people with your face and good character.

- Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "And do not turn your cheek away from people": he said: "taswir al-khadd" is tyranny and arrogance toward people and belittling them.

- Ibn Wakic related to us, he said: my father related to us, from Abu Makin, from 'Ikrima, he said: it is aversion.

Others said: He only forbade him from doing that toward someone between whom and himself there is "sa'r" (estrangement/ill feeling), not in the manner of arrogance.

Mention of those who said that:

- Ibn Wakic and Ibn Humayd related to us, both said: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding "And do not turn your cheek away from people": he said: a man who has a grudge (hunna) between himself and his brother, sees him and turns away from him.

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Abu Ahmad related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid regarding His words: "And do not turn your cheek away from people": he said: it is the man who has a grudge (hanna) between himself and his brother, so he turns away from him.

Others said: it is "al-tashdiq" (excessive, affected speech).

Mention of those who said that:

- Ibn Wakic related to us, he said: my father related to me, from Ja'far al-Razi, from Mughira, from Ibrahim, he said: it is al-tashdiq.

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Abu Ahmad related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from al-Mughira, from Ibrahim, he said: it is al-tashdiq or al-tashaddqq ["al-Tabari is in doubt"].

- Yahya ibn Talha related to us, he said: Fudayl ibn 'Iyad related to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, with its like.

* *

And His words: "wa-la tamshi fi al-ard marahan" (And do not walk upon the earth exultantly).

He says: do not walk upon the earth self-deluded (mukhtalan).

As in:

- I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: "And do not walk upon the earth exultantly": he says: with pride/vanity (al-khuyala').

- Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada regarding His words: "And do not turn your cheek away from people, and do not walk upon the earth exultantly; indeed, Allah does not like everyone self-deluded and boastful": he said: He forbade him from arrogance; His words, "Indeed Allah does not love every self-deluded one" means: arrogant, possessing boasting.

As in:

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us, and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His words: "every self-deluded, boastful one": he said: arrogant.

* *

And His words: "fakhur" (boastful).

He said: he enumerates what Allah has given, and he does not thank Allah.

**The meaning of His words: ﴿And be moderate in your pace and lower your voice; indeed, the most unpleasant of voices is the voice of donkeys﴾ [31:19]**

He means: be humble in your walk when you walk, do not be arrogant, do not hasten, but be deliberate.

The interpreters of the Qur'an (ahl al-ta'wil, "the people of interpretation") said things similar to what we have said, though some of them said that He commanded him to be humble in his walk, while others said that He commanded him to avoid hurrying in it.

*Mention of those who said that He commanded him to be humble in his walk:*

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, saying: Abu Hamzah related to us, from Jabir, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And be moderate in your pace﴾, that he said: "Humility."

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And be moderate in your pace﴾, that he said: "He forbade him from arrogance."

*Mention of those who said that He forbade him from haste:*

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak related to us, from Abdullah ibn Uqbah, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, regarding His words ﴿And be moderate in your pace﴾, that he said: "From haste."

* * *

*On His words: ﴿And lower your voice﴾*

He means: lower your voice, and make it moderate when you speak.

As related:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And lower your voice﴾, that he said: "He commanded him to moderation in his voice."

* Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿And lower your voice﴾: "Lower your voice."

The interpreters differed regarding His words ﴿Indeed, the most unpleasant of voices is the voice of donkeys﴾. Some of them said: its meaning is, "Indeed, the most ugly of voices."

*Mention of those who said that:*

* Ibn Bashshar and Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, both saying: Ibn Abi Adi related to us, from Shu'bah and Aban ibn Taghlib, both saying: Abu Mu'awiyah related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding ﴿Indeed, the most unpleasant of voices﴾, that he said: "Indeed, the most ugly of voices ﴿is the voice of donkeys﴾."

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Indeed, the most unpleasant of voices is the voice of donkeys﴾, meaning: "The most ugly of voices is the voice of donkeys. Its beginning is a groan (zafir) and its end is a sob (shahiq). He commanded him to moderation in his voice."

* Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Mu'ammal related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, saying: I heard al-A'mash say: ﴿Indeed, the most unpleasant of voices﴾ [[There may be a lacuna in it; the original is: "i.e., the most ugly of voices is the voice of ... etc."]] the voice of donkeys.

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: Indeed, the most evil of voices.

*Mention of those who said that:*

* I was told by Yahya ibn Wadih, from Abu Hamzah, from Jabir, from Ikrimah and al-Hakam ibn Utaybah, regarding ﴿Indeed, the most unpleasant of voices﴾, that he said: "The most evil of voices."

Jabir said: al-Hasan ibn Muslim said: "The most severe of voices."

* Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿Indeed, the most unpleasant of voices is the voice of donkeys﴾: "If raising the voice were good, He would not have assigned it to donkeys."

The most correct of these opinions in interpretation is the view of the one who said: its meaning is, "Indeed, the most ugly or the most evil of voices." This is like their saying, when they see an ugly face or a hideous appearance: "How unpleasant is the face of so-and-so, and how unpleasant is his appearance!"

As for His words ﴿the voice of donkeys﴾, the word "voice," which is singular, is attributed to "donkeys," which is plural. This is for one of two reasons: if you wish, you may say that "voice" carries the sense of a collective noun, as in His words ﴿would have taken away their hearing﴾ [2:20]; and if you wish, you may say that "donkeys" carries the sense of the singular, because the singular in such a context conveys what the plural conveys.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 31, verse 20:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Have you not seen that Allah has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and has amply bestowed upon you His favours, outwardly and inwardly? Yet among mankind is he who disputes concerning Allah without knowledge or guidance or an illuminating Book.﴾

His saying, the Exalted, meaning: ﴿Have you not seen﴾, O people, ﴿that Allah has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens﴾ of sun, moon, stars and clouds, ﴿and whatever is on the earth﴾ of animals, trees, water, sea and ships, and other benefits. All of that runs for your benefits and interests, for your nourishment, sustenance, provision and pleasures; you enjoy some of it and benefit from all of it. ﴿And He has amply bestowed upon you His favours, outwardly and inwardly﴾.

The reciters differed concerning the reading of this. Some of the Meccans and the majority of the Kufans recited ﴿wa-asbagha ʿalaykum niʿmatahu﴾ in the singular (niʿmah), and they interpreted its meaning as Islam, or as the testimony that there is no god but Allah. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra recited ﴿niʿamahu﴾ in the plural (niʿam, collective), and they interpreted its meaning as the blessings which Allah subjected to His servants from what is in the heavens and the earth, citing as evidence for the soundness of their reading His saying: ﴿thankful for His blessings﴾ [16:121], saying: this is the plural of niʿam.

The correct view concerning this, in our opinion, is that both are well-known readings among the reciters of the provinces, close in meaning, because niʿmah may mean the singular and may mean the collective, and the collective may include the singular. His Majesty said: ﴿If you should count the favour of Allah, you could not enumerate it﴾ [14:34], and it is known that He did not mean one favour by that. And He said in another place: ﴿He was not among the polytheists, thankful for His blessings﴾ [16:120–121], so He used the plural. Whichever of the two readings the reciter uses, he is correct.

His saying: ﴿ẓāhiratan﴾

He means: manifest upon the tongues in speech, and upon the bodies and limbs of the body in action.

* *

His saying: ﴿wa-bāṭinah﴾

He means: and hidden in the hearts, in belief and knowledge.

* *

His saying: ﴿Yet among mankind is he who disputes concerning Allah without knowledge or guidance or an illuminating Book﴾

His saying, the Exalted, meaning: among mankind is he who disputes concerning the Oneness of Allah and the sincere obedience and worship of Him, ﴿without knowledge﴾ from him concerning what he disputes, ﴿or guidance﴾: he means, nor any clarification by which he makes clear the soundness of what he says, ﴿or an illuminating Book﴾: he means, nor any revelation from Allah that came with what he claims, clarifying the truth of his claim.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 31, verses 21–22:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Follow what God has sent down," they say, "No, we will follow what we found our fathers upon." Even though Satan is calling them to the punishment of the Blaze?﴾ (21)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And when it is said to these people who dispute about the Oneness of God out of ignorance of God's greatness, "Follow, O people, what God has sent down to His Messenger, and believe in it, for it distinguishes between the one of us who is right and the one who is false, and separates the astray from the guided," they say, "No, we will follow what we found our fathers upon of religions, for they were people of truth." God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿Even though Satan is calling them﴾ by adorning for them the evil of their deeds, and their following him in their error and their disbelief in God, and their abandoning the following of what God sent down in His Book to His Prophet, ﴿to the punishment of the Blaze﴾, meaning: the punishment of the Fire which blazes and flares up.

* *

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿And whoever submits his face to God while being a doer of good has grasped the most trustworthy handhold. And to God is the outcome of all matters.﴾ (22)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And whoever makes his face devoted, humbling himself in servitude, affirming His divinity, ﴿while being a doer of good﴾, meaning: while being obedient to God in His command and His prohibition, ﴿has grasped the most trustworthy handhold﴾, meaning: he has grasped the most secure cord, which one who holds fast to it does not fear breaking. This is an image; what is meant by it is that he has grasped, through his submitting his face to God while doing good, the pleasure of God, such that he does not fear, with it, the punishment of God on the Day of Resurrection.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu al-Sawda', from Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughira, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿And whoever submits his face to God while being a doer of good has grasped the most trustworthy handhold﴾, he said: "There is no god but God."

* *

As for His words: ﴿And to God is the outcome of all matters﴾

Meaning: to God returns the final outcome of every matter, its good and its evil, and He is the one who will question its people about it and recompense them for it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 31, verses 23–26:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And whoever disbelieves, let not his disbelief grieve you. To Us is their return, and We will inform them of what they did. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of the contents of the breasts﴾ [31:23] —

He, the Exalted, says: And whoever disbelieves in Allah, let not his disbelief grieve you, and do not let yourself be consumed with regret over them. Indeed, their return and their final destination on the Day of Resurrection is to Us, and We will inform them of their corrupt deeds that they did in this world, then We will repay them for them, their recompense. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of the contents of the breasts﴾ means: Indeed Allah has knowledge of what their breasts conceal of disbelief in Allah and of preferring obedience to Satan.

* *

And His saying: ﴿We will let them enjoy themselves briefly﴾ [31:24]

means: We will give them respite in this world, a brief respite, during which they enjoy themselves. ﴿Then We will compel them toward a severe punishment﴾ means: Then We will drive them, against their will, into a harsh punishment, and that is the punishment of the Fire, we seek refuge in Allah from it and from deeds that draw near to it.

* *

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they would surely say, "Allah." Say, "Praise be to Allah." But most of them do not know﴾ [31:25] ﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. Indeed, Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy﴾ [31:26] —

He, the Exalted, says: And if you asked these polytheists among your people, O Muhammad, ﴿"Who created the heavens and the earth?" they would surely say, "Allah." Say, "Praise be to Allah."﴾ He, the Exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad: When they say that, then say to them: Praise belongs to Allah, who created that, not to one who creates nothing while they themselves are created. Then He, the Exalted, says: ﴿But most of them do not know﴾ means: But most of these polytheists do not know to whom praise belongs, nor where the place of thanks is. "Al-Hamid" means: the one praised for the blessings He has bestowed upon His creation.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 31, verse 27:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿And if whatever trees are on the earth were pens, and the sea, replenished by seven more seas after it, the words of Allah would not be exhausted. Indeed, Allah is Mighty and Wise.﴾

He, may He be exalted and remembered, says: Even if all the trees of the earth were cut into pens, ﴿and the sea [had ink], replenished by seven more seas after it﴾ — that is, the sea has ink. The pronoun in His words ﴿yamudduhu﴾ (replenishes it) refers to the sea.

* *

As for His words: ﴿replenished by seven more seas after it, the words of Allah would not be exhausted﴾

In this statement there is an elided element, which the apparent meaning makes known: it means that if the words of Allah were written with those pens and that ink, the pens would break and the ink would run out, yet the words of Allah would not be exhausted.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said similar to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said so:

Yaqub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Abu Raja', who said: I asked al-Hasan about this verse, ﴿And if whatever trees are on the earth were pens﴾. He said: If the trees of the earth were made into pens, and the seas were made into ink, and Allah said: Indeed, of My command is such-and-such, and of My command is such-and-such, the water of the seas would run out and the pens would break.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: al-Hakam narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, regarding His words: ﴿And if whatever trees are on the earth were pens﴾. He said: If they were cut into pens and the sea were ink, then with those pens and that ink ﴿the words of Allah would not be exhausted﴾, even if it were replenished by seven seas.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His words: (And if whatever trees are on the earth were pens, and the sea, replenished by seven more seas after it, the words of Allah would not be exhausted). He said: The polytheists said: This is merely speech that is about to run out. He said: Even if the trees of the land were pens, and with the sea seven more seas, the wonders of my Lord, His wisdom, His creation and His knowledge would not be exhausted.

It is mentioned that this verse was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concerning a dispute that the Jews had with him.

Those who said so:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: A man from the people of Mecca narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas: that the rabbis of the Jews said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Medina: O Muhammad, tell us about His words: ﴿And you have been given of knowledge only a little﴾ — do you mean us or your people? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed (not both), but only [some]." They said: Do you not recite in what has come to you: We were given the Torah, in which is the clarification of everything? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, it is little in the knowledge of Allah, and with you is of that what suffices you." So Allah revealed to him, regarding what they had asked him about: ﴿And if whatever trees are on the earth were pens, and the sea, replenished by seven more seas after it, the words of Allah would not be exhausted﴾. That is, the Torah's share in this is little compared to the knowledge of Allah.

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from Ikrimah, who said: The People of the Book asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the spirit, so Allah revealed: ﴿They ask you about the spirit. Say: The spirit is of the command of my Lord, and you have been given of knowledge only a little﴾. They said: You claim that we have been given only a little knowledge, while we have been given the Torah, which is wisdom — ﴿and whoever is given wisdom has certainly been given much good﴾. He said: Then this was revealed: ﴿And if whatever trees are on the earth were pens, and the sea, replenished by seven more seas after it, the words of Allah would not be exhausted﴾. He said: What you have been given of knowledge by which Allah has saved you from the Fire and admitted you to Paradise is abundant and good, yet it is little in the knowledge of Allah.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, from some of his companions, from Ata' ibn Yasar, who said: When ﴿And you have been given of knowledge only a little﴾ was revealed in Mecca, meaning the Jews, and when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) migrated to Medina, the rabbis of the Jews came to him and said: O Muhammad, has it not reached us that you say: ﴿And you have been given of knowledge only a little﴾? Do you mean us or your people? He said: "Indeed, I meant [both]." They said: You recite that we have been given the Torah, and in it is the clarification of everything. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It is little in the knowledge of Allah, and Allah has given you what, if you act upon it, you will benefit." So Allah revealed: ﴿And if whatever trees are on the earth were pens, and the sea, replenished by seven more seas after it ...﴾ until His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Hearing, Seeing﴾.

The readers differed concerning the recitation of His words: ﴿and the sea, replenished by seven more seas﴾. The majority of the readers of Medina and Kufa recited ﴿wal-bahru﴾ (and the sea) in the nominative, as a new sentence. The readers of Basra recited it in the accusative, conjoining it to "mā" in His words ﴿whatever [trees] are on the earth﴾. Whichever of the two a reader recites is correct in my view.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Mighty and Wise﴾

He says: Indeed Allah is possessed of might in His retribution against those who associate others with Him and claim with Him another god, and He is wise in His management of His creation.

The Interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Your creation and your resurrection are only like that of a single soul. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Seeing.﴾ (31:28)

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Your creation and your resurrection, O people, are not, with respect to Allah, except like the creation of a single soul and its resurrection. That is because nothing is beyond Allah's power when He wills it, and nothing He wishes is withheld from Him. ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ So the creation and resurrection of one soul is the same as the creation and resurrection of all of them.

Ahl al-ta'wil (the people of interpretation, i.e., the exegetes) said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us. And al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿like a single soul﴾, he said: "Be, and it is," for the few and the many.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: ﴿Your creation and your resurrection are only like that of a single soul﴾. He said: He says: Allah creates all of mankind and resurrects them only as He creates a single soul and resurrects it. It is correct to say "only like a single soul," meaning "only like the creation of a single soul," because the omitted element is a verb indicated by His saying ﴿your creation nor your resurrection﴾. The Arabs do this with verbal nouns (masadir), and from it is Allah's saying: ﴿Their eyes rolling like one who has fainted from death﴾, meaning: like the rolling of the eyes of one who has fainted from death; the rolling and the eyes were not mentioned because they are described.

His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Seeing﴾.

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Indeed Allah is Hearing of what these polytheists say and fabricate against their Lord, of their claims that He has associates and equals and of their other speech and the speech of others, Seeing of what they and others do of deeds, and He will recompense them for that with their due recompense.

The discussion on the interpretation (ta'wil) of His, the Exalted's, statement:

﴿Have you not seen that Allah causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night, and has subjected the sun and the moon, each running to a specified term, and that Allah is Aware of what you do?﴾ (29)

His, the Exalted's, statement means: "Have you not seen, O Muhammad, with your own eyes, that Allah causes the night to enter into the day," meaning He adds to the day what has been lost from the hours of the night, "and causes the day to enter into the night," meaning He adds to the night what has been lost from the hours of the day.

As follows:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His statement: ﴿Have you not seen that Allah causes the night to enter into the day﴾: "the decrease of the night into the increase of the day," ﴿and causes the day to enter into the night﴾: "the decrease of the day into the increase of the night."

* *

His statement: ﴿and has subjected the sun and the moon, each running to a specified term﴾

His, the Exalted's, statement means: He has subjected the sun and the moon for the benefit and interests of His creation. ﴿Each running﴾ means: all of that runs by His command until a known time and a limited term, when, upon reaching it, the sun and the moon will be wound up (and cease).

The exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) have said in agreement with what we have said.

Those who said this:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His statement: ﴿and has subjected the sun and the moon, each running to a specified term﴾: "For all of that there is a single, known time, which it does not exceed or pass."

* *

His statement: ﴿and that Allah is Aware of what you do﴾

It means: Indeed Allah, with regard to your deeds, O people, whether good or evil, is All-Knowing and Aware; nothing of them is hidden from Him, and He will recompense you for all of that. This statement was addressed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), while its intended audience is the polytheists. That is because He, the Exalted, by His statement ﴿that Allah causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night﴾, drew attention to the place of His proof, as a rebuke to those who ignore His greatness and associate others with Him in worship. This is shown by His statement: ﴿That is because Allah is the Truth, and what they call upon besides Him is falsehood﴾.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 31, verses 30–31:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿That is because Allah is the Truth, and what they call upon besides Him is falsehood, and because Allah is the Most High, the Most Great﴾ (30)

May His remembrance be exalted, says: This which I have informed you of, O Muhammad, that Allah did it, from His causing the night to enter into the day and the day into the night, and other than that of His great power, He did it only because He is Allah in truth, not what these polytheists call upon besides Him, and because none is able to do that besides Him, and divinity is fitting only for the one who does that by His power.

And His saying: ﴿And that what they call upon besides Him is falsehood﴾ means, may His remembrance be exalted: And because what these polytheists worship besides Allah is the falsehood that vanishes, perishes and comes to nothing. ﴿And that Allah is the Most High, the Most Great﴾ means, may His remembrance be exalted: And because Allah is the Most High, that is, the One possessing supremacy over everything, and everything below Him is humbled and submissive to Him; the Great, before whom everything beneath Him is diminished.

* *

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿Do you not see that the ships sail in the sea by the favor of Allah, that He may show you of His signs? Indeed in that are signs for every patient, grateful one﴾ (31)

May His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: Have you not seen, O Muhammad, that ships sail in the sea as a favor from Allah upon His creation? ﴿That He may show you of His signs﴾ means: that He may show you of His lessons and proofs against you. ﴿Indeed in that are signs for every patient, grateful one﴾ means: Indeed in the sailing of the ships in the sea is evidence that Allah, who causes them to sail, is the Truth, and that what they call upon besides Him is falsehood. ﴿For every patient, grateful one﴾ means: for everyone who restrains himself from the prohibitions of Allah and thanks Him for His favors, and so does not disbelieve in them.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: Mutarrif used to say: Among the most beloved of Allah's servants to Him is the patient, grateful one.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, who said: Patience is half of faith, and gratitude is half of faith, and certainty is the whole of faith. Have you not seen His saying: (Indeed in that are signs for every patient, grateful one), and ﴿Indeed in that are signs for those who are certain﴾, and ﴿Indeed in that are signs for those who believe﴾.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mughirah, from al-Sha'bi, regarding ﴿Indeed in that are signs for every patient, grateful one﴾, he said: Patience is half of faith, and certainty is the whole of faith.

If someone says: How did He specify this indication as being a sign for the patient, grateful one, rather than all of creation? It is said: Because patience and gratitude are among the acts of those possessing intellect and reason, so He informed that in that are signs for everyone who has reason, since the signs Allah made as lessons for those possessing intellect and discernment.
