The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 31, verse 32:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿When a wave covers them like shadows, they call upon Allah, sincerely devoting religion to Him. But when He delivers them to the land, some of them are moderate. And none rejects Our signs except every treacherous ingrate.﴾

Exalted is He, says: When those who call upon idols and images besides Allah are covered in the sea by a wave like shadows, when they have boarded ships, [the wave is] "like shadows," and "shadows" is the plural of "ẓullah." The wave is likened to them in its intense darkness, due to the abundance of water. Al-Nabigha Banu Ja'da said, describing the sea:

*It keeps pace with them, a green one with shadows,*
*on its edges, fragments of wine jars.* [[The verse is in (Majaz al-Qur'an by Abu 'Ubayda, p. 191b). He said, explaining His words (when a wave covers them like shadows): "its singular is ẓullah. Its meaning: from the intensity of the darkness of the abundance of water and its mass. Al-Nabigha al-Ja'di said, describing the sea: 'yumashihinna... fallaq al-dinan.' He means: the sea extends along with them in their journey. The 'shadows' of the sea are its waves, because they rise and shade the ship and those in it. Al-Dinan, with the unpointed dal, is the plural of dann, which is the large wine jar." (Translator's note omitted.)]]

He likened the wave, which is singular, to "ẓulal," which is a collective noun, because the wave comes one part after another, and parts of it ride upon one another in the form of shadows.

* *

As for His words: ﴿They call upon Allah, sincerely devoting religion to Him.﴾

Exalted is He, says: When a wave like shadows covers these people, and they fear drowning, they turn to Allah in supplication, sincerely devoting obedience to Him, associating none with Him at that time, calling upon no one besides Him, and seeking help from no other.

* *

As for His words: ﴿But when He delivers them to the land﴾

Meaning: from the drowning and destruction they feared at sea, to the land. ﴿So some of them are moderate﴾ means: some of them are moderate in their speech and their acknowledgment of their Lord, while nevertheless harboring disbelief in Him.

The people of ta'wil (interpretation) have said similarly to what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, he said: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith told me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words: ﴿So some of them are moderate﴾ he said: "Moderate in speech, while being a disbeliever."

* Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said concerning His words: ﴿So some of them are moderate﴾ he said: "The moderate one is the one who is in a state of righteousness regarding the matter."

* *

As for His words: ﴿And none rejects Our signs except every treacherous ingrate﴾

Exalted is He, says: And none disbelieves in Our proofs and evidences except every one who betrays his covenant. In the language of the Arabs, *al-khatr* is the worst treachery, and from it comes the saying of 'Amr ibn Ma'dikarib:

*And if you had seen Abu 'Umayr,*
*you would have filled your hands with treachery and deceit.* [[The verse is in (Majaz al-Qur'an by Abu 'Ubayda, p. 191b), where in explaining His words (kullu mukhtarin kafur) he said: "al-khatr: arrogance and treachery." 'Amr ibn Ma'dikarib said: "And you, if you had seen..." the verse. In (Lisan al-'Arab, kh-t-r): al-khatr resembles treachery and deception; it is said to be deception itself, and it is said to be the worst and most abominable treachery. Khatara, yakhturu, so he is khatir, and khattar is for emphasis. The verb is from the patterns ḍaraba and naṣara.]]

* *

As for His words: ﴿Ungrateful﴾

Meaning: denying the blessings, not thankful for the favor bestowed upon him.

The people of ta'wil have said similarly regarding the meaning of *khattar*.

Mention of those who said this:

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Hakkam narrated to us, from 'Anbasa, from Layth, from Mujahid, concerning ﴿every treacherous ingrate﴾ he said: "every treacherous betrayer."

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, he said: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith told me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words: ﴿every treacherous﴾ he said: "treacherous."

* Ya'qub and Ibn Waki' told me, they both said: Ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan, concerning His words: ﴿And none rejects Our signs except every treacherous ingrate﴾ he said: "treacherous."

* Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, concerning His words: (And none rejects Our signs except every treacherous ingrate). Al-khattar: the treacherous one; every treacherous one who breaks his pledge, ungrateful to his Lord.

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words: ﴿And none rejects Our signs except every treacherous ingrate﴾ he said: "every deniero, ingrate."

* Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said concerning His words: ﴿And none rejects Our signs except every treacherous ingrate﴾ he said: "The khattar is the treacherous one, as you say: 'ghadarani' (he betrayed me)."

* Ibn Waki' narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us, from Mis'ar, he said: I heard Qatada say: "The one who betrays his covenant."

* He said: al-Mihribi narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, he said: "The treacherous one."

* He said: My father narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Samur ibn 'Atiyya al-Kahili, from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, he said: "Deceit is treachery, and treachery is disbelief."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 31, verse 33:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord and dread a Day when no father will avail his son at all, nor will a son avail his father at all. Indeed, the promise of Allah is true, so let not the worldly life delude you, and let not the Deceiver delude you concerning Allah.﴾ (33)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: O polytheists of Quraysh, fear Allah, and dread that His wrath will descend upon you on a Day when no father will avail his son and no son will avail his father at all, for the matter on that Day will be in the hand of One who cannot be overcome, and intercession and means will be of no benefit with Him, except for a means of righteous deeds that one has sent ahead in this world.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, the promise of Allah is true﴾

He says: Know that the coming of this Day is true, for Allah has promised His servants, and His promise cannot be broken. ﴿So let not the worldly life delude you﴾ means: Let not the adornment and pleasures of the worldly life deceive you, so that you incline toward it and abandon preparation for what will save you from Allah's punishment on that Day.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And let not the Deceiver delude you concerning Allah﴾

He says: Let no deceiver deceive you concerning Allah. The word al-gharur (with the ghayn pronounced with a fatha) refers to anything that deceives a person, whatever it may be, whether it is Satan, a human being, or the world. As for al-ghurur (with the ghayn pronounced with a damma), it is a verbal noun from the speaker's saying: "gharartuhu ghururan" (I deceived him, deception).

The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) said things similar to what we have said regarding the meaning of His saying: ﴿And let not the Deceiver delude you concerning Allah.﴾

Those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us. And al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿al-Gharur﴾, he said: "Satan."

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: ﴿And let not the Deceiver delude you concerning Allah﴾: "That is Satan."

⁕ It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh al-Fadl ibn Khalid al-Marwazi say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿al-Gharur﴾: "Satan."

Some of them interpreted al-Gharur as follows:

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak related to us, from Ibn Lahi'ah, from Ata' ibn Dinar, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding His saying: ﴿And let not the Deceiver delude you concerning Allah﴾: "It is that you commit disobedience and wish for forgiveness."

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah has knowledge of the Hour, and He sends down the rain, and He knows what is in the wombs, and no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Acquainted.﴾

The Exalted says: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord and dread a Day when no father will avail anything for his son, nor will a son be at all availing for his father﴾ — it is coming to you. Its knowledge of its coming to you is with your Lord; no one knows when it will come to you. It will not come upon you except suddenly, so beware of it lest it overtake you suddenly while you remain in your misguidance, not turning back from it, so that you become, through the punishment and retribution of Allah, subject to that which you have no power to withstand. The Exalted began the report about His knowledge of the coming of the Hour. The meaning, as I have mentioned, is indicated by the context of the speech, so He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah has knowledge of the Hour﴾ — the Hour in which the Resurrection occurs; no one knows that except Him. ﴿And He sends down the rain﴾ from the sky; no one is able to do that except Him. ﴿And He knows what is in the wombs﴾ — the wombs of females. ﴿And no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow﴾ — meaning: no living soul knows what it will do tomorrow. ﴿And no soul knows in what land it will die﴾ — meaning: no living soul knows in what land its death will be. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Acquainted﴾ — meaning: indeed, He who knows all of that is Allah alone, to the exclusion of every other; He has knowledge of everything, nothing is hidden from Him, and He is Acquainted with what is and what has been.

The people of interpretation have said things similar to what we have said regarding its interpretation.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Indeed, Allah has knowledge of the Hour﴾: He said: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "My wife is pregnant; inform me what she will bear. Our land is barren, so inform me when the rain will descend. I know when I was born; inform me when I will die." So Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, Allah has knowledge of the Hour, and He sends down the rain ...﴾ to the end of the surah. Mujahid used to say: These are the keys of the unseen which Allah mentioned: ﴿And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them except Him.﴾

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding ﴿Indeed, Allah has knowledge of the Hour ...﴾, the verse: these are matters of the unseen which Allah has kept to Himself; He has not made them known to any angel brought near, nor to any sent prophet. ﴿Indeed, Allah has knowledge of the Hour﴾, so no one among people knows when the Hour will come — in which year, or which month, or night, or day. ﴿And He sends down the rain﴾, so no one knows when the rain will descend, whether by night or by day. ﴿And He knows what is in the wombs﴾, so no one knows what is in the wombs: male or female, red or black, or what else? ﴿And no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow﴾ — good or evil; and you do not know, O son of Adam, when you will die. Perhaps you will be the dead tomorrow, perhaps you will be the afflicted tomorrow. ﴿And no soul knows in what land it will die﴾ — no one among people knows where his resting place on earth will be, whether at sea, on land, in a plain or on a mountain. Exalted and blessed is He.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, from al-Sha'bi, who said: 'A'ishah said: Whoever claims that anyone knows the unseen except Allah has lied and has uttered the greatest slander against Allah. Allah said: ﴿None in the heavens and the earth knows the unseen except Allah.﴾

Ya'qub narrated to us, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Yunus ibn 'Ubayd, from 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, that a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, is there among knowledge a knowledge you have not been given?" He said: "You have been given much knowledge and good knowledge," or as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said; then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited this verse: ﴿Indeed, Allah has knowledge of the Hour, and He sends down the rain ...﴾ to ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Acquainted﴾ — none knows them except Allah, blessed and exalted.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: 'Amr ibn Muhammad narrated to me, from his father, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The keys of the unseen are five," and then he recited these verses: ﴿Indeed, Allah has knowledge of the Hour ...﴾ to its end.

'Ali ibn Sahl narrated to me, saying: Mu'ammal narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Abdullah ibn Dinar, that he heard Ibn 'Umar say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The keys of the unseen are five, none knows them except Allah: ﴿Indeed, Allah has knowledge of the Hour, and He sends down the rain, and He knows what is in the wombs ...﴾" the verse; then he said: "None knows what is in tomorrow except Allah, none knows when the rain will descend except Allah, none knows when the Hour will be established except Allah, none knows what is in the wombs except Allah, and no soul knows in what land it will die."

Ibn Wakf' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from 'Abdullah ibn Dinar, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The keys of the unseen are five, none knows them except Allah: Indeed, Allah has knowledge of the Hour, and He sends down the rain, and He knows what is in the wombs, and no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Acquainted."

Ibn Wakf' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, from Mis'ar, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from 'Abdullah ibn Salamah, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: Everything your Prophet ﷺ was given except the knowledge of the five unseen matters: ﴿Indeed, Allah has knowledge of the Hour, and He sends down the rain, and He knows what is in the wombs, and no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die﴾.

Ibn Wakf' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Khalid, from 'Amir, from Masruq, from 'A'ishah, who said: Whoever tells you that he knows what is in tomorrow has lied. Then she recited: (And no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow).

He said: Jarir and Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Abu Khabbab, from Abu Zur'ah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Five none knows except Allah: ﴿Indeed, Allah has knowledge of the Hour, and He sends down the rain ...﴾ the verse."

Abu Shurahbil narrated to me, saying: Abu al-Yaman narrated to us, saying: Isma'il narrated to us, from Ja'far, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from 'Abdullah ibn Salamah, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: Everything has been given to your Prophet except the five keys of the unseen; then he recited this verse: ﴿Indeed, Allah has knowledge of the Hour ...﴾ to its end.

It has been said: ﴿bi-ayyi ardin tamūt﴾ (in what land it will die). There is another reading: ﴿bi-ayyati ardin﴾. Whoever says ﴿bi-ayyi ardin﴾ dispenses with marking the feminine in ﴿ayy﴾ because the feminine of "ard" (land) is already present; whoever says ﴿bi-ayyati ardin﴾ makes ﴿ayy﴾ feminine, saying: ayy may be used alone with what it is attached to, so the feminine marker is needed, as in the speaker's saying: "I passed by a woman," and it is said to him: "bi-ayyatin"; and "I passed by a man," and it is said to him: "bi-ayyin." It is said: "Which woman came to you," and "Which woman came to you" (with the feminine form).

End of the commentary on Surat Luqman.
